A group G is poly-torsion-free abelian (PTFA) if it admits a finite subnormal series
1=G_0 ◁ G_1 ◁ ⋯ ◁ G_m=G
in which every quotient G_{j+1}/G_j is torsion-free abelian. The trivial group is PTFA, using the length-zero series. The term “subnormal” means each G_j is normal in G_{j+1}; normality in all of G is not required.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring ([[def-commutative-ring]]) and let $G$ be a group
([[def-group]]). The **group ring** $R[G]$ is the free left $R$-module on the
set $G$ ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]).

For each $g \in G$, write $[g] \in R[G]$ for the standard basis vector indexed
by $g$. Thus every element of $R[G]$ has a unique expression
$$\sum_{g \in F} r_g [g]$$
with $F \subseteq G$ finite and $r_g \in R$.

The notation is deliberately that of **formal** finite sums: at this stage
$R[G]$ is only the underlying free $R$-module with its distinguished basis. The
multiplication satisfying
$$[g][h]=[gh]$$
and the resulting $R$-algebra structure are constructed in
[[thm-group-ring-is-a-unital-algebra-with-basis-g]].

derivations.claim: Fix the finite subnormal series in [F1]. The base case G=1 gives QG=Q, a field and hence a left and right Ore domain.

The induction step must show that if QG_j is an Ore domain, then adjoining the torsion-free abelian quotient G_{j+1}/G_j through the possibly nonsplit group extension preserves the no-zero-divisor and Ore properties. The proof of this extension step is not supplied by the preceding base case or by formal polynomial-ring arguments.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, let $B^4=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:\lVert x\rVert^2\le1\}$ with boundary $S^3$. The oriented connected sum $K\#K^\dagger$ bounds a smooth properly embedded disk $D\subset B^4$ for which the squared radial function $\rho(x)=\lVert x\rVert^2$ restricts to a Morse function on the interior of $D$ with all critical points of index $0$ or $1$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. On oriented ambient-isotopy classes of smooth knots in $S^3$, the connected-sum operation is associative and commutative, and the standard unknot is a two-sided identity. Here “commutative monoid” means a set with an associative binary operation, a two-sided identity, and equality after interchanging the two inputs.

Fix a coordinate orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ for the mirror convention. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere. A connected-sum datum consists of one smoothly embedded closed three-ball around a short subarc of $K$ and one around a short subarc of $J$, each meeting its knot in a single trivial properly embedded arc, together with the fixed standard orientation-reversing boundary identification of the two standard oriented ball boundaries that joins the oriented arcs into one circle. Choose this standard map once in the standard two-ball model so that it commutes with $r$ and an orientation-preserving half-turn interchanging the two balls preserves the joining convention. Here a trivial arc is an embedded interval in a ball that is carried by an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of ball-arc pairs to a straight diameter. Remove the interiors of the two balls and glue the remaining boundary spheres using this fixed identification; the resulting oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere is a connected sum of $K$ and $J$, denoted $K\#J$ for the specified datum.

The **standard unknot** is the oriented unit circle in a fixed coordinate two-plane of $S^3\subset\mathbb R^4$. A knot is **nontrivial** if it is not ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $S^3$ to the standard unknot. A nontrivial knot is **prime** if it has no connected-sum presentation whose two summand knots are both nontrivial.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

The reverse-mirror construction in [F2] supplies an inverse annulus in the standard 4-ball, hence in the standard product, and so it is admissible in all four categories.

For C_ex and C^{1/n}, transitivity and compatibility of boundary connected sum must be checked against the specified ambient homeomorphism and R_n-homology conditions. The definitions in [F1] alone do not prove these gluing properties, and the smooth and topological arguments in steps 1.1–1.2 do not supply the missing verification.

Let $V=S^1\times D^2$ be the standard oriented solid torus, with oriented core $S^1\times\{0\}$. A **pattern** is a smooth oriented knot $P$ contained in the interior of $V$, together with a chosen closed tubular neighbourhood $N(P)$ contained in the interior of $V$. Its **winding number** $w(P)$ is the integer by which the homology class $[P]$ maps to $H_1(V;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ under the isomorphism that sends the oriented core to $1$. The **pattern exterior** is $X_P=V\setminus\operatorname{int}N(P)$; its **outer torus** is $\partial V$ and its **inner torus** is $\partial N(P)$. A **companion** is a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$ with a specified orientation-preserving tubular embedding $e:V\to S^3$ that sends the core to $K$ and identifies the solid-torus meridian and product longitude with the positive meridian and preferred longitude of $K$. The **satellite knot** $P(K)$ is $e(P)$, with chosen exterior $E_{P(K)}=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}e(N(P))$; the image $e(\partial V)$ is its **companion torus**. The outer torus is **incompressible** when it bounds no properly embedded disk in $X_P$ with essential boundary on $\partial V$. It is **product-parallel** to the inner torus when $X_P$ is a product $T^2\times[0,1]$ with those tori as its ends. This definition alone asserts neither incompressibility nor essentiality of the companion torus.

derivations.claim: Represent K#J by placing K and J in disjoint 3-balls and joining the removed arcs by a product band. Choose the zero-framed tubular neighborhood so its meridian and preferred longitude restrict to the corresponding meridians and longitudes on both sides of the separating sphere.

Insert P into that neighborhood and cut along the separating sphere. Inside the K-ball the inserted tangle is exactly the arc of P with K tied into it, which is the pattern P_K. The remaining J-ball is the companion neighborhood for P_K(J). Gluing along the separating annulus matches the same meridian and preferred longitude, so the two constructions are related by an orientation-preserving isotopy of the glued knots.

Tying a local knot into an arc contained in a 3-ball does not change the homology class of P in the solid torus. Its core coefficient, and hence its winding number, is unchanged. This proves both claims.

middle form. Let $M$ be a closed oriented smooth manifold of dimension $4k$,
$k\ge0$, and let $Q_M$ be its middle-dimensional intersection form on
$H^{2k}(M;\mathbb R)$ ([[def-middle-dimensional-intersection-form]],
[[lem-middle-dimensional-intersection-form-is-symmetric-and-nondegenerate]]).

([[def-definiteness-inertia-and-signature-data-over-the-reals]]): $p$ the
maximal dimension of a positive-definite subspace, $q$ the maximal dimension of
a negative-definite subspace, and $z$ the dimension of the radical. By
Sylvester's law of inertia ([[thm-sylvesters-law-of-inertia]]) these integers
are intrinsic to $Q_M$ and $p+q+z=\dim_{\mathbb R}H^{2k}(M;\mathbb R)$. The
**signature** of $M$ is
$$\sigma(M):=p-q\in\mathbb Z.$$

[[lem-middle-dimensional-intersection-form-is-symmetric-and-nondegenerate]], so
$z=0$ and $p+q=\dim_{\mathbb R}H^{2k}(M;\mathbb R)$; the signature can

diagonal entries in any basis diagonalizing $Q_M$. For $k=0$ the group

signed count of components, so $\sigma(M^0)$ is the number of positively
oriented components minus the number of negatively oriented components, and
$\sigma(\varnothing)=0$.

value is assigned in other dimensions (see the closing bookkeeping remark on
this page). The value is independent of the chosen diagonalizing basis and of

For a smooth oriented knot K in S³, let e_K:V→S³ be a zero-framed tubular embedding carrying the core to K and carrying the meridian and product longitude to the positive meridian and preferred longitude of K. The satellite knot P(K) is e_K(P).

When concordance preservation has been established, the formula [K]↦[P(K)] defines a set map on each of C_sm, C_top, C_ex and C^{1/n}. The solid-torus meridian is strong winding number ±1 for P if, after V is embedded as the standard unknotted solid torus and P(U) denotes the resulting closure, that meridian normally generates π₁(S³\P(U)). Normal generation means that the smallest normal subgroup containing the element is the whole group. Strong winding number ±1 is a separate condition from ordinary winding number ±1. No additivity or homomorphism property is part of this definition.

Let P be an oriented pattern of winding n≠0 and K an oriented knot. If P(U) bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth 4-manifold B with boundary S³ and H_i(S³;R_n)→H_i(B;R_n) is an isomorphism for every i, then for every K the zero surgeries M(P(K)) and M(K) are smoothly R_n-homology cobordant, with preferred meridian carried to preferred meridian. Let knots be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented S³ and let I=[0,1]. Let C_sm be their smooth concordance classes, where equivalence is witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in S³×I. Let C_top be their locally flat topological concordance classes in that product. Let P be a pattern and let K be a knot. Form a pattern P_K by tying K into a small arc of P in a ball disjoint from the solid-torus core, using the zero framing. For every knot J, the satellite P(K#J) is isotopic as an oriented knot to P_K(J). The pattern P_K has the same winding number as P.

Removing A×D² and attaching D²×S¹×I along the annular side, with ∂D² matched to the annulus longitude and the core matched to the normal meridian, produces a cobordism V from M(K₀) to M(K₁). Let P be a pattern of strong winding number ±1. For every oriented knot K, regard P(K) as the pattern obtained by tying K into each strand of P in the companion solid torus. sign(X)=sign(W₀)−sign(W₁)
and
sign_Γ^(2)(X)=sign_Γ^(2)(W₀,ψ₀)−sign_Γ^(2)(W₁,ψ₁).

Let X be a closed oriented smooth 4-manifold, Γ a discrete group, and φ:π₁(X)→Γ a homomorphism. Then the von Neumann signature of the NΓ-coefficient intersection form equals the ordinary signature:
sign_Γ^(2)(X,φ)=sign(X).

derivations.claim: Glue W₀ to −W₁ along their identified boundary M. The boundary representations agree, so ψ₀ and ψ₁ glue to a homomorphism on the fundamental group of the closed oriented 4-manifold X=W₀∪_M(−W₁).
